interpretation.equation: K_RR*x_R + sum_g K_R,E_g*x_E_g = B_R up to saved full-equation residual; K_RR*y_fixed=B_R up to fixed-system residual.
interpretation.contribution: z_g=solve(K_RR,-K_R,E_g*x_E_g); sum_g z_g reconstructs x_R-y_fixed up to saved equation defects, product/solve and summation roundoff.
interpretation.groups: Five saved logical beams, each split into all body displacement/rotation coordinates vs all local velocity/angular-rate coordinates. Internal-force/moment and reaction columns excluded only after exact retained-row zero tests.
interpretation.yaw: Actual saved W times retained yaw coordinate102 (full2208), per native F3 file setting. No extra input scaling.
interpretation.closure: Record full109-state and yaw closure error; predeclared relative diagnostic gate1e-9 with state-scale or gross-contribution normalization, no absolute1 floor. This is an algebraic consistency check, not a physics acceptance or rigorous forward-error certificate.
interpretation.product_envelopes: gamma_(16*n+32)*abs(K_group)@abs(x_group)+tiny enclosures describe forcing arithmetic only. GECON is a condition estimate, not a rigorous inverse bound; closure error is not attributed solely to summation.
limitations: Algebraic contributions of the saved full elastic state through a chosen retained resolvent, not causal effects or independent physical subsystem transfer functions.
Signed groups may strongly cancel; rank by magnitude is descriptive, not a percentage of causal importance.
No change to physical parameters, source equations, operating point, trim, full matrix assembly or original harmonic gates; no experimental-validation or convergence claim.
Only seven predeclared saved-grid samples; no adaptive frequency search or extra solve.

body_convention.conclusion: At the three selected dip-region points (1, 1.09648 and 1.15738 Hz), complex changes are only 0.0370–0.0526%. The coefficient change does not resolve the discrepancy there. The largest selected change is 5.94% at 8.90352 Hz.

findings.conclusion: Section offset compliance matches steady equations 18–20; rotating current resultants and dr cross N retain loaded-state geometric terms. No demonstrated omitted-prestress term.
SO(3) objective midpoint differs from documented ASWING discrete averaging; this is an explicit parity question, not by itself a defect.
Fin c=+x,s=+z,n=-y: lateral bending EIcc, vertical-span torsion GJ. Boom c=-y,s=+x,n=+z, equal EIcc/EInn. No swapped-axis evidence.
Literal fin-root y offset of +1 ft is preserved by rigid-joint translation and moment transfer; no structural rudder hinge supplied.
Documented zero section inertia defaults are honored; distributed-position inertia and Ccg effects remain. Dynamic quadrature does not duplicate the standalone segment correction.
Sign and time ordering match unsteady equations 57–59. Literal tdeps and tdgam are absent/zero, so no material damping change is justified for this case.
Natural-cubic endpoint parity remains unspecified by public guide; midpoint material sampling retains finite-mesh error. Neither has been shown to cause the yaw feature.

limits: No structural defect demonstrated is not a validation of Daedalus or original ASWING.
No per-beam attribution inferred from magnitude curves or changed-shape constraints.

primary_reference_review.scope: Primary lateral/structural reference research; no model changes, reconstruction, numerical validation or fitted parameters.
primary_reference_review.conclusion: NASA-CR-183305 provides a directly relevant Light Eagle lateral-flexibility mechanism and loaded free-free modal reference data, but not a matched operating point or complete exact reconstruction of the current Daedalus literal model. The current yaw dip remains unexplained quantitatively.

findings.equation: tau_aero = 3.3*c/(2*U_inf), as reported. A first-order lag is inserted between rudder deflection and the control contribution to lateral force/roll/yaw torque.
findings.applicability: Mechanistic evidence for delayed flexible tail/wing response; not a measured material-damping constant or a fit target for current dae.asw. No added lag or damping is proposed.

findings.statement: The design couples wing bending stiffness and lift-wire length/stiffness to loaded dihedral; high-speed torsional washout reduces dihedral and rudder-only roll-yaw authority.
findings.applicability: An independent loaded-shape design check relevant to the current declared6.7m/s study. It does not supply the Bode point, a precision measured displacement, tailboom EI/GJ distribution or a modal pass threshold.

findings.statement: Much dynamics testing used unpowered glides to avoid1.5–2Hz pedalling contamination. The fitted lag model is explicitly phenomenological and restricted to similar aerodynamic-control maneuvers; it is not a flutter/gust model.

Visual scan inspection exposes ambiguous/inconsistent printed Wagner/filter and aerodynamic-lag pole notation. No questionable OCR coefficients/signs or pole units were adopted. The report records the prose estimates and the dimensionally explicit tau relation, not a new implemented transfer function. Table3-2 approximate mode labels must not override the numbered mode-shape drawings.

coverage.search: Exact textual NASA-CR-183305, Light Eagle, Zerweckh, and R. Bryan Sullivan search over docs/validation/*.md and *.json found no named existing reference benchmark. Numeric substring matches were excluded as unrelated.
coverage.status: Existing Daedalus work checks mesh/speed/directional derivatives and changed-model elastic suppression; it does not establish this NASA modal/flight-test comparison. Existing Pazy/ST/Durrant work has different models and conditions.

next_scope: Use the already authorized saved elastic-contribution decomposition to identify which kinematic groups participate in the current dip; this is algebraic participation, not causal attribution.

Before any independent structural test, make a mapping sheet for the NASA Light Eagle/Daedalus labeling, element dimensions/materials, pilot/lumped mass, free-free boundary conditions,1g preload and apparent-mass convention.

If that mapping remains incomplete, publish a separate conditional reference model rather than changing literal dae.asw. Compare loaded deformation and modal shapes/frequencies as independent quantities; do not tune to the rudder dip.

Keep the current rudder-Bode comparison explicitly unmatched in operating point and not mesh converged. The natural-mode numbers and lag estimates neither resolve its amplitude discrepancy nor validate its step response.
